message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"12.16","text":"However, so that these things might happen in this way, I devised the fabrication of a dream, as though someone had stood beside me at night and said, “Woman, leave the city immediately with your twin children for a time, until I tell you to return here, for you will suddenly die a terrible death together with your husband and all your children.” All the same, I did so. For as soon as I falsely told my husband about the dream, he himself became terrified and sent me by sea to Athens, together with my two sons, male and female servants, and a considerable amount of money, so that I might educate my sons, “until,” he said, “the one who gave the revelation decides that you should return to me.” Yet while I, wretched as I am, was sailing with my children, I was driven into these parts by unruly winds; when the ship broke apart in the night, I suffered shipwreck. After everyone else had died, I alone, unfortunate woman that I am, was swept along by a fierce wave and thrown onto a rock. Seated on it, wretched as I was, I did not cast myself into the deep, because I hoped to find my children alive—not even then, when my soul was intoxicated by the waves and I could easily have done it.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐπενόησα ὄνειρον πλάσασθαι","chosen":"I devised the fabrication of a dream","rationale":"The phrase means that she deliberately conceived a plan to fabricate a dream, not that she merely interpreted or experienced one."},{"source_quote":"ὁμῶς","chosen":"all the same / yet","rationale":"The contexts support a concessive transition. “Likewise” is lexically possible for the printed form but is less suitable here."},{"source_quote":"τῷ χρηματίσαντι","chosen":"the one who gave the revelation","rationale":"χρηματίζω here concerns the supernatural communication in the alleged dream; alternatives include “the one who gave the warning” or “the one who delivered the oracle.”"},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ ἀνέμων ἀταξίας","chosen":"by unruly winds","rationale":"Literally, the wording evokes being driven by the disorder or unruliness of winds."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ πέτρας ἐρρίφην, ἐφ’ ἧς","chosen":"thrown onto a rock. Seated on it","rationale":"πέτρας is read as genitive singular after ἐπί, agreeing with singular ἧς; reading it as accusative plural would create a number mismatch."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ψυχὴν μεμεθυσμένην τοῖς κύμασιν","chosen":"my soul was intoxicated by the waves","rationale":"The rendering preserves the metaphor of the soul made drunk or overwhelmed by the waves."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"12.17","text":"However, when daybreak came, I kept looking around, crying loudly and wailing mournfully, searching for the dead bodies of my unfortunate babies. The local people took pity on me. Seeing that I was naked, they first clothed me and then searched the deep for my children. When they found none of what they were seeking, some of the hospitable women approached me for the sake of comfort, and each recounted her own troubles, so that through the shared experience of similar misfortune I might find comfort—which in fact grieved me even more. For I said that I was not so wicked as to find comfort in the misfortunes of others. Although many offered to take me in as a guest, one poor woman from this place pressed me so insistently that she compelled me to come to her own shelter. She said to me, “Take courage, woman. My husband too was a sailor and died at sea while still in the bloom of youth. Since then, although many have sought me in marriage, I have chosen to remain a widow because I long for my husband. Whatever both of us can procure by the work of our hands will be shared between us.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῶν ἐμῶν ταλαιπώρων βρεφῶν","chosen":"my unfortunate babies","rationale":"βρέφη denotes infants or very young children; “babies” retains that force rather than harmonizing it with the earlier designation “sons.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸν βυθὸν ἀνηραύνων","chosen":"searched the deep","rationale":"The local people search the sea’s depth for the missing children; “searched the bottom” is another possible rendering."},{"source_quote":"οὐ γὰρ ἔφην οὕτω κακὴ εἶναι","chosen":"I was not so wicked","rationale":"In context she rejects taking pleasure or comfort from others’ suffering, so κακή has a moral sense. “So miserable” is lexically possible but less coherent with the following clause."},{"source_quote":"εἰς ξενίαν πολλῶν με ἄγειν ἀξιουσῶν","chosen":"although many offered to take me in as a guest","rationale":"ξενία refers to hospitality or lodging for a stranger; the wording may also be rendered “many asked to bring me into their homes.”"},{"source_quote":"ἐν τῇ νεαζούσῃ τυγχάνων ἡλικίᾳ","chosen":"while still in the bloom of youth","rationale":"The phrase describes the husband as being at a youthful age when he died."},{"source_quote":"ἃ διὰ χειρῶν ἀμφότεραι πορίζειν δυνάμεθα","chosen":"whatever both of us can procure by the work of our hands","rationale":"διὰ χειρῶν points to what they can obtain through their own manual labor."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"12.18","text":"And, so that I do not prolong for you words that are unnecessary, I lived with her because of her devotion to her husband. Before long, my hands—wretched woman that I am—were paralyzed by attacks of biting pain, and the woman who had taken me in, her whole body bound by some affliction, lay prostrate at home. Since, then, the compassion of the women from before had waned, and both I and the woman at home were incapacitated, for many years I have sat here, as you see, begging; and whatever I manage to obtain, I also carry home as food for my fellow sufferer. So much for my own affairs; let them have been told sufficiently. What remains is that you are preventing the fulfillment of your promise to give me the drug, so that I may give it to her as well, since she desires to die, and in this way I too may be able to depart from life, as you said.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"διὰ τὴν φιλανδρίαν","chosen":"because of her devotion to her husband","rationale":"φιλανδρία denotes love of or devotion to a husband. The immediate context favors the poor widow’s devotion, though the phrase could encompass the narrator’s corresponding marital devotion."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τῶν δηγμάτων παρείθησαν","chosen":"were paralyzed by attacks of biting pain","rationale":"δήγματα literally denotes bites or stings and can describe sharp, biting pains; a more literal alternative is “were disabled by the bites.”"},{"source_quote":"ὅλη ὑπὸ πάθους τινὸς συνδεθεῖσα","chosen":"her whole body bound by some affliction","rationale":"ὅλη indicates that the affliction affected her wholly, while συνδεθεῖσα retains the image of being bound."},{"source_quote":"ἀμφότεραι ἐπισινεῖς τυγχάνομεν","chosen":"both ... were incapacitated","rationale":"ἐπισινεῖς can mean harmed, impaired, or afflicted; here it describes both women as unable to support themselves normally."},{"source_quote":"ὧν ἂν εὐπορήσω","chosen":"whatever I manage to obtain","rationale":"εὐπορέω here concerns securing available resources rather than being generally wealthy."},{"source_quote":"τὸ φάρμακον","chosen":"the drug","rationale":"φάρμακον can mean medicine, drug, or poison. “Drug” preserves the lexical breadth, while the expressed desire for death supplies the lethal purpose in context."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ζῆν ... μεταλλάξαι","chosen":"depart from life","rationale":"The construction is a euphemism for dying, literally involving a change or departure from living."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"12.19","text":"When the woman had said this, Peter seemed, amid many thoughts, to stand suspended. I came up and said, “I have been going around looking for you for a long time. What are we to do now?” Peter instructed me to go on ahead and wait for him at the boat. Since there was no contradicting him when he gave an order, I did what had been commanded. But Peter, his heart throbbing with a faint suspicion—as he himself related everything to me later—questioned the woman, saying, “Tell me, woman, your origin and city and the names of your children, and I will give you the drug at once.” She was caught under pressure, unwilling to tell him but eager to receive the drug, so she contrived to say one thing in place of another. Even so, she said that she herself was an Ephesian and that her husband was a Sicilian; she likewise changed the names of all three children. Peter, thinking that she was telling the truth, said, “Alas, woman! I thought that today would be a day of great joy, because I suspected that you were a certain woman—the one I thought you were—whose circumstances I have heard and know exactly.” She adjured him, saying, “I beg you, tell me, so that I may know whether there is any woman more miserable than I am.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ λογισμῶν πολλῶν ὁ Πέτρος μετέωρος ἐδόκει ἵστασθαι","chosen":"Peter seemed, amid many thoughts, to stand suspended","rationale":"μετέωρος preserves an image of being suspended or unsettled; idiomatic alternatives include “stood perplexed” or “was lost in thought.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸ γένος καὶ τὴν πόλιν","chosen":"your origin and city","rationale":"γένος may refer to family, people, nationality, or origin. “Origin” leaves the scope open alongside the more specific request for her city."},{"source_quote":"βίαν πάσχουσα","chosen":"caught under pressure","rationale":"The phrase depicts her as constrained by conflicting pressures: reluctance to disclose the truth and desire to obtain the drug."},{"source_quote":"ἐσοφίσατο ἄλλα ἀντὶ ἄλλων εἰπεῖν","chosen":"she contrived to say one thing in place of another","rationale":"The idiom describes an ingenious evasion or lie while retaining the source’s wording pattern."},{"source_quote":"ὁμῶς ἔφη","chosen":"Even so, she said","rationale":"The context requires a concessive sense: despite her reluctance, she supplied false information. “Likewise” is possible for the printed form but does not fit the progression as well."},{"source_quote":"ὑποπτεύσας σὲ τινὰ εἶναι, ἣν ἐνόμιζον","chosen":"because I suspected that you were a certain woman—the one I thought you were","rationale":"The deliberately repetitive rendering preserves Peter’s guarded identification. A smoother alternative is “suspecting you were someone I had in mind.”"}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"12.20","text":"And Peter, who did not know how to lie, began out of compassion for her to tell the truth: “A certain person accompanies me, now already a young man, a Roman citizen who desires teachings about reverence for God. He tells me how, though he has a father and two twin brothers, he sees none of them. ‘For my mother,’ he says, ‘as my father used to tell me, saw a dream and left the city of the Romans for a time with her twin children, so that she would not die by an evil fate; and after leaving with them, she has not been found.’ The husband of this woman—who is the young man’s father—also went away in search of her and has not been found.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ψεύδεσθαι οὐκ εἰδὼς","chosen":"who did not know how to lie","rationale":"The phrase describes Peter as unpracticed or incapable in lying, not merely as unaware that a particular statement was false."},{"source_quote":"λοιπὸν ἤδη νεανίας ὢν","chosen":"now already a young man","rationale":"λοιπὸν ἤδη marks his present stage of life. Alternatives include “by now a young man” and “now at last a young man.”"},{"source_quote":"τῶν τῆς θεοσεβείας ὀρεγόμενος λόγων","chosen":"who desires teachings about reverence for God","rationale":"θεοσέβεια is piety or reverence directed toward God, while λόγοι here denotes words, discourses, or teachings."},{"source_quote":"ἥ τε γὰρ μήτηρ (φησίν), ὡς ὁ πατὴρ διηγεῖτό μοι","chosen":"‘For my mother,’ he says, ‘as my father used to tell me’","rationale":"The rendering treats μοι as retained first-person wording within the young man’s embedded report. A formally indirect alternative, “his mother ... as the father told me,” would make “me” refer to Peter, which is contextually difficult."},{"source_quote":"τὴν Ῥωμαίων πόλιν","chosen":"the city of the Romans","rationale":"The rendering preserves the source’s descriptive expression rather than replacing it silently with the conventional name “Rome.”"},{"source_quote":"κακῷ μόρῳ τελευτήσῃ","chosen":"die by an evil fate","rationale":"μόρος denotes fate, doom, or the death allotted by fate; “meet a terrible death” is a smoother alternative."},{"source_quote":"ὁ δὲ ταύτης μὲν ἀνήρ, αὐτοῦ δὲ πατὴρ","chosen":"The husband of this woman—who is the young man’s father","rationale":"The paired description identifies the same person in relation first to the woman and then to the accompanying young man."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
